We compare five policy scenarios: driving restrictions,

congestion pricing, 
subway expansion, and combinations of subway expansion with one of the other 
two policies. The first two scenarios represent two types of ­demand-side policies: 
a ­command-and-control approach and

a ­market-based approach, respectively.

of demand- and ­supply-side policies. The first scenario follows the actual driving

restriction policy implemented in Beijing: a vehicle is prohibited from driving one 
day a week. For congestion pricing, we calibrate a ­distance-based charge (at ¥1.13/
